newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Jerusalem groundbreaking in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Jerusalem groundbreaking in two weeks.

text.p: An aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said a controversial project approved on Wednesday to build housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem could begin in about two weeks.

"It will probably take, if I know the bureaucracy, about two weeks for it to be translated from a government decision into action in the field," aide David Bar-Illan told CNN. "I presume that the bulldozers will be there within a week or two."

Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told reporters a ministerial committee on Jerusalem approved the construction of 6,500 homes for Jews, with 2,500 to be built in the first stage. Another 3,000 housing units would be built for Arabs.
The homes will go up at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel, a tree-covered hill taken by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. The site is between Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
Bar-Illan said the new homes would alleviate a housing shortage in East Jerusalem. Palestinians, however, called the project an attempt by Israel to cement its hold over all of the city.
Palestinians have warned the project could touch off anti-Israeli violence in the West Bank and Gaza reminiscent of clashes in September in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed.
